blockers.quote: You know your number now. And you don't look up.
blockers.why: Check #11. The scene direction already shows you not looking up: face down at the page, chip out of focus at the edge of the frame. 'And you don't look up' narrates the picture. It also leans toward summing the film up just before the last image.

suggestions.quote: So that one in a thousand counts people who never turned up. It's a crowd's number, not a verdict on you.
suggestions.fix: So that one in a thousand? It counts people who never showed up. A crowd's number. Not yours.

suggestions.quote: Your own chip started from a crowd too. Last year, over 9 lakh people applied for UPSC's civil services exam. And 958 got in (c01). About one in a thousand.
suggestions.fix: Add say.yaml entries: '9 lakh' = 'nine lakh', '958' = 'nine hundred and fifty-eight', 'UPSC' = 'U-P-S-C'. Split it into two breaths: 'Your chip started from a crowd too. Last year, over nine lakh people applied for the civil services exam.' / 'Nine hundred and fifty-eight got in. About one in a thousand.'

suggestions.quote: And yours? Here's the number nobody puts on a coaching poster. Of the people who reached last year's interview room... about one in three got in (c03).
suggestions.fix: Cut it into three takes so it fits in breaths: 'And yours? Here's the number nobody puts on a coaching poster.' / 'Of the people who reached last year's interview room...' / 'about one in three got in.'

suggestions.quote: So. Leave the bat where it is, and keep following the biggest number? Or give it back, and let him choose?
suggestions.fix: Too long for one breath. Split it: 'So. Leave the bat where it is, and keep following the biggest number?' [beat] 'Or give it back... and let him choose?'

suggestions.quote: You've done to him exactly what you did to yourself. You let a number pick his life.
suggestions.fix: It reads like a verdict, and a little like a teacher. Keep the first sentence [low] and drop the second, or shrink it to 'A number picked.' so the dark gap under the cupboard carries the weight.

suggestions.quote: Row three. Your own notes this time. And the chip... stirs.
suggestions.fix: No emotion is marked for this line in the notes. Add [hushed, a small hope], with a breath before 'stirs'.

suggestions.quote: At home, Aarav's waiting. A fee slip for a cricket academy. And one question, for the one who can see the numbers.
suggestions.fix: Add the direction [warm, a little uneasy]. Trim the last sentence to 'And one question. For the one who can see the numbers.' so it can be spoken.

suggestions.quote: But his tiny number follows you into the hall. So you look for certainty. The teacher.
suggestions.fix: Add the direction [dry, a touch rueful]. Make 'The teacher.' its own short take.
Read as three separate takes, [hushed], with 'Zero.' dropping in pitch. The held note covers the rest. Don't add anything after it.

keep.quote: One chair. Out of two thousand five hundred.
You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
